notes:
**A LinkedIn page is no longer reported as a broken link.**

LinkedIn answers automated requests with HTTP 999 — a status code it invented,
which does not exist in the standard. Docket read anything at or above 400 as a
dead page, so a school's own LinkedIn profile was listed as a broken outbound
link it should update or remove. The page is fine.

The control that settles it: `linkedin.com/school/harvard-university/` returns
999 as well, to a browser as much as to a crawler, while
`linkedin.com/company/microsoft/` returns 200 to both. The code describes the
request, not the page.

Any status outside the range HTTP actually defines — 100 to 599 — now reads as
"could not be checked" rather than "broken". A vendor inventing a status code
is telling you about its own policy, and that is not something you can fix by
editing your links. A connection that never completes is still reported as
broken, because that genuinely is about reachability, and an ordinary 404 still
means gone.
